bookTitle: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis

facts.statement: Markets spend roughly 70 percent of their time moving sideways in congestion consolidation channels and only 30 percent of their time actively trending, serving as the spawning grounds where major trends are born.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Price Congestion (Sideways Market): A period where price action moves sideways in a consolidation range... Markets spend roughly 70% of their time moving sideways in congestion and only 30% actively trending.

facts.statement: Sideways price congestion is generated by three primary market catalysts: pending fundamental economic news releases, insider accumulation or distribution climaxes, and old historical price areas trapping weak market participants.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Three Catalysts for Sideways Congestion: Pending Fundamental News Releases, Insider Accumulation & Distribution Phases, Old Price Traps.

facts.statement: Support and resistance is a lagging technical tool focusing on past price history, whereas Volume Price Analysis is a leading tool anticipating future moves; combining them creates a comprehensive three-dimensional framework.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Leading vs. Lagging Analysis: Support and resistance is a lagging technical tool because it relies on past price history. Volume Price Analysis is a leading tool that anticipates future moves.

facts.statement: An isolated pivot high is defined by a 3-bar reversal pattern where the central candle posts a higher high and a higher low than the candles immediately to its left and right, marking the upper ceiling.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Isolated Pivot High (Resisting Ceiling): A 3-candle sequence where the central candle posts a higher high and a higher low than the candles immediately to its left and right.

facts.statement: An isolated pivot low is defined by a 3-bar reversal pattern where the central candle posts a lower low and a lower high than the candles immediately to its left and right, marking the lower floor.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Isolated Pivot Low (Supporting Floor): A 3-candle sequence where the central candle posts a lower low and a lower high than the candles immediately to its left and right.

facts.topic: The Common Sense and Leeway Rule
facts.statement: If a congestion phase forms without posting a clean 3-bar pivot high or low on one side, traders should rely on visual price action, volume density, and common sense rather than waiting rigidly for indicator confirmation.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The Common Sense & Leeway Rule: Pivots are visual indicators. If a congestion phase forms without posting a clean 3-bar pivot... traders should rely on visual price action, volume density, and common sense.

facts.statement: Support and resistance boundaries are pliable rubber bands with elastic give rather than rigid steel walls, allowing price to temporarily tick slightly beyond a ceiling or floor without invalidating the range.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Pliable Rubber Bands, Not Rods of Steel: Support and resistance levels are not rigid walls; they act like elastic rubber bands with a degree of 'give'.

facts.statement: A valid market breakout requires a decisive candle close past the S/R boundary with a visible clear water gap, supported by well-above-average and rising volume to reflect institutional effort.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Rules for a Valid Clean Breakout: The 'Clear Water' Requirement... Strong & Rising Volume... Low-Volume Pullback Retests... Boundary Role Reversal & Stop Loss Protection.

facts.statement: If price breaches a support or resistance boundary on low or below-average volume, it signals a lack of institutional participation and represents a classic insider fakeout designed to flush retail stops.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Low-Volume Fakeouts (Insider Traps): If price breaches a boundary on low or below-average volume, it signals a lack of institutional participation... classic insider 'trap moves'.

facts.statement: Coulling compares price structures to a multi-story house where ascending price breaks a ground-floor ceiling to turn it into a floor of support, and descending price turns a broken floor into a ceiling of resistance.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The House Analogy (Floors & Ceilings): Visualizing a vertical cross-section of a house... once a ceiling is breached, it flips to become a floor of support.

facts.statement: Forcing price away from a congested price zone of trapped orders requires massive volume effort, acting similarly to dragging a heavy object out of deep, sticky quicksand.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Quicksand / Dragging Someone from a Bog: Dragging a heavy object out of quicksand requires enormous physical effort; similarly, forcing price away from a congested zone requires massive volume effort.

facts.statement: On a GBP/USD 15-minute chart, an economic news release catalyzed a wide-spread bullish candle closing firmly above a 70-bar congestion ceiling with clear water and ultra-high volume, validating the fundamental news and trend continuation.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Case Study 1: GBP/USD 15-Minute Chart (Extended Congestion Breakout)... economic news release provided the catalyst... wide-spread bullish candle closed firmly above the ceiling with 'clear water', accompanied by ultra-high volume.

generalAssumptions: Market price manipulation is structurally transparent on the volume tape.
Effort versus result governs institutional capital movement.
